Riley (Manager): quick q — if someone on my team uses the company backup childcare credit but then goes on parental leave the next week, can they roll unused credit into the leave period or next month?
Asha (People Ops): short answer: generally no, credits are per-calendar-month but there are a couple exceptions. do you have dates?
Riley (Manager): yeah parent starts leave 2026-04-09, used half the credit in March, wondering if we can apply remaining to April while they're on leave.
Asha (People Ops): ok noted. policy: backup childcare credit covers same-month childcare only. unused portion doesn't auto-rollover. exception: if the leave start is unplanned (medical/emergency) we can review for a one-time pro-rated payout — needs manager + docs.
Riley (Manager): how do we file that review?
Asha (People Ops): submit an "Emergency Childcare Exception" request via the benefits portal, include start date and a short note. form id: BCK-42. attach receipts if you want payroll to do a one-time reimbursement.
Devon (Eng): also curious — if they plan to work part-time during leave (phased return), can they still use credit pro-rated?
Asha (People Ops): yes — if they're active on payroll for any hours in the month, they remain eligible for that month's credit pro-rate. we'll calculate based on hours reported.
Sam (Payroll): payroll note: reimbursement requests with receipts must be in by the 5th of the following month to hit that month's payroll cycle. if you miss cutoff we can do an off-cycle manual, but it takes longer and needs finance approval. use expense code `PARENT-BCK` on the form.
Riley (Manager): good to know. what about holiday overlap? parent is off Easter Monday 2026-04-06 then leave starts Thu 04-09.
Asha (People Ops): holidays don't change credit eligibility; treat each calendar month separately. with those dates they'd be eligible for April's pro-rate only if working hours reported in April.
Benefits Bot: https://benefits.redwood.example/portal/forms/BCK-42 — Emergency Childcare Exception form (requires manager approval + optional receipts).
Devon (Eng): for coverage planning, what's the recommended handoff for their on-call weeks? want to make sure we coordinate.
Asha (People Ops): recommend a 2-week overlap where possible, documented in the team runbook. if on-call is critical, open a temporary headcount or contractor backfill request via `#eng-ops` and mark it `parental-coverage`.
Riley (Manager): super helpful. i'll submit BCK-42 with the dates and tag payroll.
Sam (Payroll): once submitted tag me @Sam and I'll flag it for the payroll cutoff. if we need manual pay we'll need the manager signoff + receipts scanned.
Asha (People Ops): checklist I'll attach here: 1) submit BCK-42 + manager approval; 2) attach receipts (if emergency payout request); 3) include leave start date and reason; 4) tag payroll for cutoff; 5) update runbook/on-call rota.
Riley (Manager): perfect, i'll do that today. thanks all :tada:
Asha (People Ops): thanks — ping me if anything is urgent, i'll shepherd the request.
Benefits Bot: Reminder scheduled: if BCK-42 is started but not approved within 3 business days a People Ops rep will follow up.
Riley (Manager): got it — closing the loop once submitted.
